title: FACET single-adapter dynamic Mirror feature-code boundary
hypothesis: On a frozen 20-task class-incremental sequence with no oracle task ID at inference, replacing native FACET task transformations with structured m preserves final mean accuracy and backward transfer within 1.0 percentage point while reducing total inference task-state bytes >=15% and keeping P95 <=1.10 native, beyond same-byte FiLM.
physical_object: one shared FACET adapter, task-conditioned feature transform and replay-free consistency regularizer
mirror_code: compact task/history m substituting only the native feature transform coefficients
native_control: FACET original single-adapter task-conditioned feature consistency with no replay
controls: native FACET with full original task conditioning and consistency loss
FACET conditioned diagonal/FiLM at matched bytes
one shared adapter plus simple task linear embedding
independent task-specific adapters as upper bound

screen.fixture: CPU initially: class-balanced 8×8 handwritten-digit feature vectors or synthetic class-incremental 20 tasks, 32-feature MLP base frozen, train stream disjoint task identities; natural ViT+FACET second stage requires verified official code, no independent paper-gain claim from toy.
steps: Construct disjoint class/task ID stream and five held-out task orders; do not reveal true task ID during inference.
Reproduce one shared adapter, native FACET task conditioner and replay-free consistency loss; keep absence of replay buffer explicit.
Replace only task transform with diagonal, low-rank ordinary embedding and m signed/Givens chart with k=2/4/8.
Use same task-identification policy and support examples for all methods; preserve feature consistency coefficients.
Log all prior-class accuracies after each task, forward/backward transfer, task-code bytes and generator FLOPs.
Run all five fresh sequences and classify M0 when native conditioner or FiLM matches.
screen.hardware: Stage1 torch CPU float32 batch 32; Stage2 1 CUDA GPU if reproducing FACET ViT; report clock, seed, support/test split and genuine native implementation status.
screen.metrics: CIL final mean accuracy, backward transfer and old-task retention, feature consistency loss, task-state actual bytes, hidden task ID leakage, latency

gates.PASS: 4/5 fresh task orders meet FACET mean and backward transfer within 1.0 pp, >=15% total learned task-state bytes saved with P95 <=1.10, and cheap same-byte FiLM control does not dominate.
gates.FAIL: Original FACET/FiLM equal or better at bytes+quality+runtime, task ID leaked or replay enabled, or toy class task not appropriate for trained-model claim.
gates.UNCERTAIN: Missing native control, audit correctness, or physical byte/time measurement

storage: serialize paid inference bases/router/task codes and metadata
compute: MAC/FLOP proxy, examples/updates, warmup and real P50/P95 calibrated seconds
